guidance.statement: GenMed business expected to return to 6-8% top-line growth with supply issues resolved
Vaccines business guided to strong high-double-digit growth
Innovative portfolio intended to reach about 10% of top-line
Bepirovirsen market authorization expected this financial year
EBITDA margins to be roughly what we were at last year in 34% kind of range for FY27
Established general medicines and vaccines business to grow 8-10% as part of the ₹8,000 Cr top-line ambition over four to five years
Blenrep launch in India in the next two to three months, most probably Q2 or Q3 FY27
Bepirovirsen launch in India in the next three quarters latest

operating_notes.text: Innovative portfolio contributed about 6% of Q4FY26 sales, up from 2% like-to-like, against a stated 10% intent.
GenMed was flat in FY26 after losing more than ₹100 Cr of sales to supply constraints; vaccines grew over 11-12%.
Oncology field force is about 25 people for solid tumours, with a hematology team being recruited for Blenrep.
Shingrix grew 65% in Q1FY27 and sells upwards of 45,000-50,000 doses a quarter; it is an INR100 crores plus brand on a MAT basis.
Blended MR productivity is INR15-16 lakh per rep, up 5-6% this quarter; oncology has about 40-45 people and does INR10 crores a month.
About 44-45% of the GenMeds portfolio is under price control; Q1 volume growth was 3-3.5% and price about 6%.

timeline.summary: On its 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call, GSK Pharma reported FY26 revenue up 2% with EBITDA margin at 34% (+290 bps) and a first-ever PAT excluding exceptionals above ₹1,000 Cr, and declared a final dividend of ₹57 per share.

On its 3 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, GSK Pharma reported standalone sales of ₹924 Cr (+15% YoY) and PAT of ₹253 Cr (+24%, about 17% excluding a Biddle Sawyer dividend), and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to roughly 34%.

watchlist.text: GenMed revenue growth returning to guided range
Market authorization for Bepirovirsen (chronic hepatitis B)
Market authorization for RSV vaccine after Subject Expert Committee approval

watchlist.response: Management said there are no supply constraints from April/Q1FY27 and that delayed vaccine shipments will shift into the June quarter.
watchlist.text: Supply constraints from the CMO fire persisted into Q4 despite earlier guidance that they were behind; analysts asked when they would normalize.

watchlist.response: Management reiterated the double-digit ambition and pointed to new launches and GenMed recovery, without giving a numeric FY27 target.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed on the gap between the stated double-digit growth ambition and 2% FY26 growth.

watchlist.response: Management said pricing is in line with standard of care (₹10-16 lakh per patient) and that margins remain undiluted, but gave no margin figure.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for specialty portfolio margins and per-patient oncology pricing.

watchlist.response: Management deferred, citing the 40 million disease burden and saying it would answer specifics in the Q2 call after completing its roadmap work; evasive on treated-patient numbers.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on how many hepatitis B patients are actually treated in India and the commercial model for Bepirovirsen (cure vs lifelong therapy).

watchlist.response: CFO said the concentration was deliberate and front-loaded before the September quarter, and S&A ratios should normalise to historical trends through the year.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether the 36% YoY opex rise is a one-off or a run-rate.

watchlist.response: MD said it is not a current priority and GSK is not part of the global trials, then said he did not know which company ran the India trial; no timeline given.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked about the 24-valent pneumococcal vaccine trial in India and whether it is an FY29 launch.
